cases.title: Lakers @ Spurs — Norm Nixon free-throw fake mishandled; protest upheld, last 3 seconds replayed, Spurs win 117-114 (Nov 30, 1982 - Apr 1983)
cases.incident_summary: With San Antonio leading 116-114 and seconds left in regulation, Lakers guard Norm Nixon faked his second free-throw attempt, drawing players from both teams into the lane. The officials called a double lane violation and ordered a jump ball (at halfcourt/center court) instead of requiring Nixon to re-shoot the free throw. The Lakers won the tap and Nixon scored the tying basket at the buzzer to force overtime; Los Angeles eventually won 137-132 in double overtime. San Antonio protested that the officials misapplied the rules; in December 1982 Commissioner Larry O'Brien upheld the protest. The final three seconds of regulation were replayed before the teams' next scheduled meeting in April 1983, and the Spurs won the replayed finish 117-114.

cases.title: Heat @ Hawks — Official scorer wrongly fouls out Shaquille O'Neal; protest upheld, final 51.9s replayed, Hawks win 114-111 (Dec 19, 2007 - Mar 8, 2008)
cases.incident_summary: The Hawks' official scoring table mistakenly credited a fourth-quarter foul (called on Udonis Haslem with 3:24 left in regulation) to Shaquille O'Neal. As a result, when O'Neal was whistled in overtime with the Hawks leading 112-111, the table ruled it his sixth foul and disqualified him — it was only his fifth. Al Horford's subsequent free throws made it 114-111. Miami protested; on Jan 11, 2008 the NBA upheld the protest (the first granted since December 1982), fined Atlanta $50,000 for 'grossly negligent' failure to follow scoring procedures, and ordered the final 51.9 seconds replayed before the teams' next meeting on March 8, 2008. Neither team scored in the replay; the official final became Hawks 114, Heat 111 in overtime (replacing the original 117-111 result).

cases.title: Kings @ Grizzlies — Courtney Lee buzzer-beater stands; Sacramento protest denied (Nov 13-28, 2014)
cases.incident_summary: With Sacramento leading 110-109 and 0.3 seconds left, Memphis inbounded via Vince Carter; Marc Gasol screened two Kings defenders and Courtney Lee scored a reverse layup at the horn for a 111-110 Grizzlies win. Sacramento protested that (a) center Ryan Hollins tipped the inbounds pass, which should have started the clock earlier, and (b) Lee's shot did not leave his hands before the buzzer. Commissioner Adam Silver denied the protest on Nov 28, 2014, finding the referees acted within their proper judgment and that no misapplication of the rules occurred. The basket and the 111-110 final stand.

cases.title: Pacers @ Lakers — Glenn Robinson III jumper inside the arc credited as a 3; corrected 108-96 to 108-95 a week later (Jan 20-27, 2017)
cases.incident_summary: With 1:49 remaining in the fourth quarter, Pacers guard/forward Glenn Robinson III made a jump shot from inside the three-point line, but the basket was incorrectly credited as a 3-point field goal. The game ended with an announced final of Lakers 108, Pacers 96. Seven days later, on Jan 27, 2017, the NBA announced the scoring error: the statistics were corrected, Robinson's scoring total was changed to five points, and the official final score became Lakers 108, Pacers 95 — a one-point correction that changed the combined total from 204 to 203. The league stated the error impacted the final score but not the final outcome.

cases.title: Timberwolves @ Pelicans — Arena scoreboard showed wrong score in final minute; Towns fouled thinking Wolves were down 7, not 8 (Dec 31, 2018)
cases.incident_summary: In the final minute of the Pelicans' 123-114 win over the Timberwolves, the in-arena scoreboard displayed an incorrect score that credited Minnesota with an extra point. With about 22 seconds left and the shot clock off, Minnesota was actually down 8 but the board suggested the deficit was 7; Karl-Anthony Towns fouled Julius Randle, who made a free throw to push the lead to 9, and Towns fouled out with about 12 seconds left. The official score was always correct — only the arena display was wrong — but the bad display appears to have changed on-court behavior and the second-half betting result (Timberwolves +second-half spread did not cover).

cases.title: NBA Finals Game 6, Warriors vs Raptors — Draymond Green corner make ruled a 2, not reviewed; stands (Jun 13, 2019)
cases.incident_summary: Late in the first quarter of Game 6 of the 2019 NBA Finals (approximately 2:15 remaining, per NBC Sports Bay Area), Draymond Green made a corner jump shot that was ruled a 2-pointer on the floor. Replays suggested he may have been behind the arc, but the play was not reviewed. The league's position, as reported by NBC Sports Bay Area, was that even if reviewed there would not have been clear and conclusive evidence to overturn the on-floor ruling of a 2-point field goal. Golden State trailed by 3 at halftime instead of a possible 2; with 9 seconds left in the game the Warriors had the ball down 1 — a span during which the un-awarded point loomed large. The ruling was never changed.

cases.title: Rockets @ Spurs — James Harden's made dunk not counted; Rockets protest denied, 135-133 2OT final stands (Dec 3-9, 2019)
cases.incident_summary: With 7:50 left in the fourth quarter and Houston leading 102-89, James Harden stole the ball and dunked it with such force that the ball cleared the net, whipped around the rim and bounced upward/out — creating the appearance of a miss. The officiating crew did not count the basket and ruled the ball out of bounds off Harden; the Rockets' attempt to challenge the call was not granted. Houston argued the made basket was worth two points and the score was recorded incorrectly (a misapplication of rules, not a judgment call). The Rockets filed a formal protest within the 48-hour window seeking to replay the final 7:50 from that point. On Dec 9, 2019, Commissioner Adam Silver denied the protest; the league disciplined the three officials for misapplying the Coach's Challenge rule and acknowledged that a properly granted replay would have shown the basket counted. The 135-133 double-overtime Spurs win stands and the two points were never added.
cases.scoring_play: James Harden (HOU) steal and dunk — physically a made basket (league later acknowledged replay would show it counted), ruled no-basket on the floor.
cases.score_before: Rockets 102, Spurs 89 (7:50 Q4) — per CNBC/USA Today. If counted, Rockets lead grows to 15 (104-89).

originally_reported.value: No basket; play ruled a miss with ball out of bounds off Harden; Rockets lead stays 102-89
originally_reported.basis: On-floor ruling Dec 3, 2019 (crew chief James Capers postgame explanation; protest reporting via USA Today, NBC Sports).

corrected_value.basis: No correction was ever applied — the basket was never added to the score. The league acknowledged the error but denied the protest.

final_official.basis: Final official result; protest denied Dec 9, 2019 (CNBC, Click2Houston/AP).

sources_disagreed: On-floor officials' ruling (no basket) vs. video evidence and the league's own post-hoc acknowledgment (basket was good)

Whether D'Antoni requested the challenge in time remains disputed between the crew and the team.

cases.title: Bulls vs Hornets — Zach LaVine assist request reviewed and NOT granted; league states postgame assist policy (Feb 9, 2022)
cases.incident_summary: In the Feb 9, 2022 Bulls-Hornets game, Zach LaVine made what appeared to be a routine assist (a chest pass to DeMar DeRozan) but was not credited with the assist. Bettors holding over-5.5-assists LaVine wagers hoped for a stat correction that never came. In response to a fan inquiry, an NBA representative wrote that assists are credited at the discretion of the arena's in-game statisticians and that NBA Operations does not credit or remove assists postgame — only assists credited to the wrong player are updated. This negative case is kept to document the boundary of the correction pipeline: judgment-call assists are final as scored in-arena.

cases.title: Warriors @ Trail Blazers — De'Anthony Melton free throw recorded as a miss, final score corrected 139-104 to 140-104 (Oct 23-24, 2024)
